subject: Hartwell pilot: footprint playbook and onboarding runway
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
To: Lisa Chang <lisa.chang@hartwell.com>, procurement@hartwell.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-09-12T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Footprint & pilot runway — quick clarifying questions

Hi Lisa / Hartwell procurement team,

Thanks again for the time yesterday. To put together a concise footprint playbook for your regulated pilot, I need a few quick clarifications so we can map Dedicated vs Private economics and a minimal safe onboarding runway: 

- Target steady-state TPS / requests per second (approx): you mentioned "moderate" — can you confirm a number range (e.g., 50–200 rps)?
- Latency SLOs: is p95 <= 150ms acceptable, or do you need tighter (e.g., p95 <= 100ms)?
- Data residency / network constraints: is VPC-only (no public endpoints) required from day one?
- Procurement window: is 6–10 weeks the right expectation?

I attached a short capacity slate (initial_capacity_slate.pdf) and our SOC2 snapshot (SOC2_snapshot.pdf) for your security team. Once you confirm the numeric targets and procurement horizon I’ll produce a two-path plan: (A) Dedicated reserved pool with a 6-week canary -> scale commit ladder, and (B) Private (VPC) onboarding timeline with MPA / audit gating and an estimated CPU/GPU footprint. I’ll also include a fallback ladder if traffic or compliance requirements shift mid-pilot.

Goal: deliver a one-page mutual action plan (MAP) and an SOW draft by next Tuesday that you can share with procurement.

Thanks — Diego
Diego Fernandez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
 diego@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

From: Lisa Chang <lisa.chang@hartwell.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@hartwell.com
Date: 2028-09-13T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Footprint & pilot runway — quick clarifying questions

Hi Diego — thanks for the follow up. A few answers below: 

- Expected steady-state: ~150 requests/sec during business hours, spikes to ~300 rps for short windows (5–10 min).
- Latency: our product team wants p95 <= 120ms if possible. p99 can be relaxed to 400ms for now.
- Data residency: yes — VPC-only for production. For an initial pilot we could accept a dedicated-hosted model if traffic and audit evidence flow through an approved tunnel.
- Procurement timeline: procurement estimates 8 weeks to sign an MPA + PO (vendor checks + security review).

Security asks: SOC2, audit logs retention (13 months), and evidence of key management integration. I reviewed SOC2_snapshot.pdf — please include details on our ability to receive per-request audit logs and log export cadence.

Can you outline a canary approach that minimizes exposure while giving us a path to either a reserved Dedicated commit or full VPC Private onboarding? If you can share a MAP and rough SOW, procurement will start the intake immediately.

Best,
Lisa Chang
Head of Integrations, Hartwell Health
lisa.chang@hartwell.com | +1 (617) 555-4422

From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
To: Lisa Chang <lisa.chang@hartwell.com>, procurement@hartwell.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-09-14T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Footprint & pilot runway — proposed two-path plan and canary

Lisa — thanks for the clear targets. I put together a two-path playbook below (summary). I attached a draft MAP (Hartwell_mutual_action_plan_v1.docx) and will follow up with the SOW.

Executive summary (short):
- Canary target: 6-week pilot, starting on Dedicated reserved capacity (to get reliable latency and metrics into your engineering reviews) with optional switch-to-Private for production after compliance gating.
- Pilot footprint (initial): 4 x A100-class GPU nodes in a dedicated pool (sustained handling of 150 rps, burst to 300 rps with autoscale buffer). Estimated KV/cache sizing and prefix caching reduce per-token GPU time — included in the attached slate.
- Private production path: VPC Private deployment with 2x the baseline GPU count (8 nodes) to account for multi-az redundancy and regulatory isolation; HSM/KMS for key management and 13-month audit log retention.

Fallback / escape ladder:
1) If pilot latency/p95 exceeds 140ms for >2 days, route traffic to a higher-performance model variant (quantized + optimized kernel) within Dedicated pool.
2) If compliance team needs private-only, we commit a staged migration: (a) snapshot export and audit handover week 3, (b) security validation week 4–5, (c) Private cutover week 6–8.

Cost delta (high level): Dedicated pilot (6 weeks): ~$45k (compute + support). Private production (monthly run rate): ~$115k/mo (includes private plane, 3-az redundancy, enterprise support). Exact numbers in proposed_pricing_breakdown.xlsx.

Ops/engineering asks for Hartwell: 1) provide a test subset of production traffic and DNAT/VPC peering window; 2) confirm model variant(s) you want for the pilot; 3) procurement readiness for a 6–9 week MAP + SOW cycle.

Marissa — can you confirm the recommended Reserved GPU months and any discount ladder we should offer for a 12/24 month commit? Vivek — can you confirm Private onboarding runway (ops milestones) and any special audit artifacts procurement will need? Priyom — once Marissa confirms pricing, can you prep a clean PO-ready summary for Hartwell procurement?

Diego
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-09-15T10:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Footprint & pilot runway — pricing and commit recommendations

Diego / team — pricing and commit suggestions below (spreadsheet attached). High level: we should offer a conservative pilot discounted rate to remove friction, plus a clear uplift if they convert to Private.

Pricing bullets:
- 6-week Dedicated pilot (4 A100-class nodes): list = $52,000; pilot discount -> customer pays $36,000 (includes 24/7 pilot support & one on-call).
- Conversion offer to Private: first 3 months at 10% off list if signed within 30 days of pilot completion. Private baseline = 8 nodes, $125k/mo list -> $112.5k/mo with early-convert discount.
- Commit ladder for Dedicated (if they prefer reserved): 12 month commit = 20% off list; 24 month = 28% off.

Contract asks to reduce procurement friction:
- Short MAP that confirms SLAs to be included in SOW (p95 targets; credits for >2% downtime).
- Audit artifact pack: SOC2 report + log export sample + KMS integration guide (we’ll hand to procurement).

Next steps (who does what):
- Priyom: draft PO summary + high-level payment terms for procurement.
- Vivek: produce Private onboarding milestone checklist (network, key rotation, audit outputs).
- Diego: share MAP + SOW draft with Lisa for procurement intake.

Marissa Cole
Senior Deal Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Lisa Chang <lisa.chang@hartwell.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@hartwell.com
Date: 2028-09-19T16:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Footprint & pilot runway — confirmation and next steps

Diego / Marissa — thanks, that all looks reasonable. Hartwell is comfortable starting with the 6-week Dedicated pilot (we accept the pilot discount). Procurement will open the intake for the MAP + SOW tomorrow; their target is to have a signed MAP and PO within the 8-week window.

We would like these items in the delivery set before kickoff:
- MAP (finalized)
- SOW draft with milestone payments tied to pilot weeks 0/3/6
- Sample log export (format + retention policy) and KMS integration checklist
- DocuSign link for the MAP and SOW (procurement prefers electronic signing)

Please send the SOW + DocuSign by EOD Monday and we’ll route to procurement. If you prefer, we can start the pilot on Dedicated while Private onboarding runs in parallel (we’ll make the final call after week 3 security validation).

Lisa
Head of Integrations, Hartwell Health
